title: Vow and Bakery
premise: August Marchetti fled the coastal town of Salt Hollow after her father's orchard empire collapsed in scandal, burying her grief in sea turtle conservation and a vow never to return. But when her estranged grandmother dies and leaves the family orchard deed to two names at once — August's and that of Elian Voss, the boy her father ruined and the man she once loved — August is dragged home into a legal tangle neither can untangle alone. As the town's new power brokers circle the orchard land for a resort development, August and Elian must co-manage a dying harvest, confront the lies their parents told them, and decide whether love is worth the price of forgiving themselves. In the end, they save the orchard by giving half of it to the town as a working commons, choosing shared roots over private victory, and marry beneath the oldest pear tree just as the first spring blossoms open.
about_author: Paloma Galloway is a former orchard hand from the Pacific Northwest who writes love stories rooted in land, family debt, and second chances. She now lives beside a cider press and a very opinionated dog named Bramley.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: August's POV. On a research vessel, August logs sea turtle nests and deflects a colleague's gentle probing about her past. A certified letter arrives: her grandmother has died and left her the Salt Hollow orchard. Emotional beat: avoidance cracking open.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Deed
chapters.summary: August's POV. Her lawyer explains the deed names her AND Elian Voss jointly — a condition her grandmother set deliberately. August refuses to go. Emotional beat: dread and denial.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Elian runs a struggling cider operation on the same land, stunned to learn August is his co-inheritor. He remembers the scandal that broke both families. Emotional beat: old resentment, new curiosity.

chapters.title: Salt Hollow Welcome
chapters.summary: August's POV. August arrives to find Elian living in her grandmother's cottage, legally. Their first confrontation is sharp and wounded. Emotional beat: friction as chemistry.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. They draft an uneasy agreement: split the harvest, sell the land, split the money, never speak of their fathers. Emotional beat: a truce built on silence.

chapters.title: The Orchard in Winter
chapters.summary: August's POV. Walking the dormant rows, August finds her grandmother's pruning journal and the first hint that the orchard's decline was engineered, not natural. Emotional beat: grief turning to suspicion.

chapters.title: The Man from Meridian
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Developer Callum Reeve makes a generous offer for the land, pressuring them to sell quickly. Elian, drowning in debt, is tempted. Emotional beat: temptation with a smile.

chapters.title: Bread and Bad Blood
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the town bakery, August learns the townspeople blame her father for Elian's family's ruin — and blames her by inheritance. Emotional beat: shame she didn't earn.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Elian finds his father's old ledgers suggesting the Marchetti scandal was staged to force a sale — to someone. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under old hatred.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Truth
chapters.summary: August's POV. August shares the pruning journal with Elian; they discover her grandmother recorded sabotage — cut roots, poisoned soil tests. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Harvest Deadline
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. The bank calls Elian's loan; if the pear harvest fails, the orchard goes to auction — and Meridian buys cheap. Emotional beat: time pressure begins.

chapters.title: Hands in the Same Soil
chapters.summary: August's POV. Working the rows side by side, they fall into an easy rhythm; August admits she counted turtles to avoid counting her losses. Emotional beat: tenderness sneaking in.

chapters.title: The Town Meeting
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Reeve pitches the resort to the town, promising jobs. The crowd splits; old friends take sides. Emotional beat: the community as a battlefield.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Letters
chapters.summary: August's POV. In the attic, August finds letters between her grandmother and Elian's mother — a friendship hidden for decades, and a shared secret about the deed. Emotional beat: the past rewriting itself.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. After a festival night and too much cider, August and Elian nearly kiss, then retreat. Emotional beat: want versus fear.

chapters.title: The Saboteur's Boot Print
chapters.summary: August's POV. They catch someone tampering with the irrigation at night; the figure escapes but drops a Meridian-branded flashlight. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Reeve's Second Offer
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Reeve offers Elian a personal payout to sign alone — enough to erase his debt. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Almost-Betrayal
chapters.summary: August's POV. August learns Elian took the meeting with Reeve and assumes the worst; she signs nothing and shuts him out. Emotional beat: trust fractured by old wounds.

chapters.title: His Mother's Voice
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Elian plays an old voicemail from his dying mother: she begged him to protect August, not punish her. He weeps in the cider house. Emotional beat: inherited hate questioned.

chapters.title: Apology, Unscripted
chapters.summary: August's POV. Elian confesses he never intended to sell and shows her the ledger evidence. August apologizes for assuming. Emotional beat: the thaw.

chapters.title: Blossom Season Begins
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. The orchard blooms early and stubbornly, as if fighting back. The town starts showing up to help, unprompted. Emotional beat: hope as collective act.

chapters.title: The Hidden Clause
chapters.summary: August's POV. The lawyer decodes the deed: the co-inheritance dissolves only if both agree to sell — or if the orchard fails. Her grandmother designed a test, not a trap. Emotional beat: understanding the dead.

chapters.title: Reeve Turns the Screws
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Reeve buys Elian's bank debt and threatens foreclosure within thirty days unless they sell. Emotional beat: the villain stops smiling.

chapters.title: The Town's Quiet Army
chapters.summary: August's POV. Neighbors organize a harvest brigade; even old enemies of the Marchettis show up. August, who swore never to belong here, is handed a cider press handle. Emotional beat: belonging, terrifying and warm.

chapters.title: Night in the Packing Shed
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Trapped by a storm, August and Elian finally speak the whole truth about their fathers — and kiss. Emotional beat: love admitted against duty's warning.

chapters.title: The Morning After the Storm
chapters.summary: August's POV. Happiness, quickly shadowed: August finds documents showing her own father, before his death, signed the first Meridian option — he was the original seller. Emotional beat: the mirror turns on her.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Man in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Elian discovers his father wasn't a victim but a willing accomplice who took payment and shame in equal measure. He must forgive a dead man to keep loving August. Emotional beat: self-forgiveness as the true battle.

chapters.title: Reeve's Leverage
chapters.summary: August's POV. Reeve leaks the Marchetti scandal to the press again, using August's father's signature to turn the town against the orchard. Emotional beat: public ruin, private steadiness.

chapters.title: The Auction Notice
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Foreclosure auction is set for harvest day. Reeve gloats. Elian proposes a desperate plan: harvest everything, prove the orchard's value, and find the original forged deed. Emotional beat: all-in.

chapters.title: Digging Up the Past
chapters.summary: August's POV. Following her grandmother's journal clues, they dig beneath the oldest pear tree and find a locked tin: the forged signature, correspondence, and proof Reeve's firm manufactured the scandal a generation ago. Emotional beat: vindication with a cost.

chapters.title: What Vengeance Costs
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. They could destroy Reeve publicly — but the evidence also implicates both their fathers, and the town's peace with it. Emotional beat: the price of truth.

chapters.title: The Harvest
chapters.summary: August's POV. The whole town harvests at dawn against the auction clock; even Reeve's hired hands defect to help. Emotional beat: communal triumph.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. At the courthouse steps, they reveal the forged deed. The auction collapses; Reeve's lender pulls out amid fraud exposure. Emotional beat: climax — power's corruption laid bare.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: August's POV. Reeve, cornered, offers to buy their silence. August refuses on the record, choosing the town's trust over a payout. Emotional beat: integrity over survival's easy math.

chapters.title: The Deed, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. August proposes deeding the orchard into a community trust — half working farm, half town commons. Elian agrees, giving up sole ownership he never wanted. Emotional beat: love expressed as shared ground.

chapters.title: Fathers, Forgiven
chapters.summary: August's POV. At their fathers' graves, August and Elian read the truth aloud together and let the hatred go. Emotional beat: mourning finished.

chapters.title: Cider and Promises
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. The town celebrates the first pressing under the new trust. Elian proposes to August beneath the oldest pear tree with his mother's ring. Emotional beat: joy earned.

chapters.title: The Turtle Season
chapters.summary: August's POV. August negotiates to keep her research post while co-managing the orchard — she no longer has to choose between selves. Emotional beat: integration.

chapters.title: Blossom Wedding
chapters.summary: August's POV, with Elian interludes. They marry at blossom time in the orchard commons, the whole town attending, the deed framed on the cider house wall. Emotional beat: fullness.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. One year later: the commons thrives, a turtle-nesting beach is protected by trust funds, and their daughter's name is added to a new deed clause — stewardship, not possession. Final beat: love as legacy, roots over walls.
